WSP Parsons Brinckerhoff and DNV GL (2015). Industrial Decarbonisation and Energy Efficiency Roadmaps to 2050 - Glass. Report and Appendices, prepared for the Department of Energy and Climate Change (DECC) and the Department for Business, Innovation and Skills (BIS), London, March 2015.

Source = Glass_Report.pdf (main, 106 printed pages) + Glass_Appendices.pdf (appendices A-D, 79 printed pages), one source; moved as wsp_2015_uk-roadmap-glass.pdf and wsp_2015_uk-roadmap-glass-appendices.pdf. Page numbers are PRINTED page numbers (footer "Page N of M"); Appendix C Table 11 is on printed pages 71-75. Loaded: UK baseline specific energy and CO2 per tonne for melting, lehr, forehearth, float bath and forming (Table 6, DECC 2014), the 1.4 MWh/t efficient large furnace, process temperatures, and the 17-option register (whole technologies electric melting, oxy-fuel, carbon capture, hydrogen in the main file; the rest in _measures with capex per representative site, TRL, adoption and CO2/electricity reduction). NOT loaded: per-option energy change (the register gives only CO2 or electricity reduction), operating costs (excluded by the study), pathway tables, social/business findings; fibre glass is out of the quantitative scope. Traps: (1) capex is per representative site and site capacity is not printed (container furnaces under 100 to over 600 t/day), so no per-t figures; (2) electric melting capex (GBP 40m) is assumed equal to a conventional furnace and its 100% CO2 reduction counts direct combustion emissions only (electricity use not given); (3) carbon capture capex covers capture alone and is oxy-combustion based (TRL 6; post-combustion TRL 7); (4) Table 6 energy is final heat energy of the process with carriers not split and no heating-value basis; (5) "(C)" in the register = CO2 reduction, "(E)" = electricity reduction; (6) the report states costs in present-day (2015) value so 2015_GBP is used; (7) the Appendix C title promises descriptions but the table has none. Process-heat end-use for lehr/forehearth is set to process-heat-high-temp for lack of a temperature class.
